Verification, Absorption, Outcome.' introduces the three names for the first time on THIS slide (not a forward pointer to a later one) and the same chunk's figure prints the identical three words as SVG text at y=44 plus the caption 'THE FAR HALF · AHEAD' — visual and textual naming in one chunk, elaborated one chunk later. 'the session you send off in this module' (raw:7) is a generic forward-looking noun phrase describing an upcoming module activity, not a pointer to a specific unnamed artifact. Closest candidate for a violation: raw:14 'crosses the wall from you to the team' — 'the wall' is not named earlier in this file (it is formally coined two modules later per the backing block's sibling-copies note), but this rule's own arc-earned-vocabulary carve-out states premature use of not-yet-earned spine vocabulary 'still fails check_writing.md §14... that's a writing-class flag, not a slides one' — so it is explicitly out of this rule's scope, and read cold the phrase is self-parsing plain metaphor defined in its own clause ('from you to the team'). No never-named, vague-with-history, or re-chunk-stranded referent inside this rule's own lane.

Scan of raw:1-15 for positional callback phrasing ('the opening lecture said', 'earlier lecture', 'this workbook', 'at the top of') -> 0 hits. raw:3 'Back to the map' names the training's own spine artifact by concept ('the map'), never by file or page position. raw:11 'So far you sat inside every loop' characterizes the whole M1-M3 arc generically, not a document referenced by position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: raw:11 'So far you sat inside every loop: you read each reply, caught each wobble as it happened' is the only backward-shaped reference in the body -- a generic characterization of the whole M1-M3 arc, not a named specific exercise/lecture beat that a re-chunk could strand. Covered by the maintainer's own dated note (raw:25, 'Module ranges in body = arc-lecture carve-out, check_lectures §3; the subject is the arc'). No 'the X you did/saw' phrasing naming one specific prior beat anywhere in the body.

Chunk 1 = figure + one self-carrying bullet (raw:7) stating a full claim ('the map lights its other side now... Verification, Absorption, Outcome'), not a bare wait-state. Chunk 2 (raw:11-15) has five bullets, each a standalone claim (felt problem, three phase definitions, one closing question). Neither is a context-dependent fragment.

raw:3 'Back to the map: the far half opens' is true of chunk 1's own content (figure shows the far half lighting, bullet states exactly that). raw:9 'Long-running work adds three new concerns' is true of chunk 2 -- three concerns follow, each bolded (Verification/Absorption/Outcome, raw:12-14); the framing bullet (raw:11) and closing question (raw:15) set up and follow from the three, they don't contradict the count.

'Not X. Not Y. Z.' -- 0 instances in raw:1-15. Anaphora/epistrophe triples -- closest candidate is the three bolded phase bullets (raw:12-14), but each opens on a different verb ('tells you' / 'determines' / 'determines') and carries distinct new content (result quality / take-up capacity / what survives) across separate list items, not a repeated-frame triple. Self-grading superlatives -- 0 instances. Number + own retraction -- the only numerals ('an hour', raw:11; 'a hundred steps', raw:15) are plain illustrative durations with no hedge/retraction pattern. Abstraction-noun stacks -- 'the gap between the two' (raw:13) names a concrete comparison (generating vs. reading/judging/merging), not an abstraction stack. Verb-triplet-with-empty-leg -- the three phase verbs sit in separate bullets, each fully fleshed with concrete content on its own.
